entries.t: If I Only Had a Brain
entries.s: If I Only Had a Brain [from One Step Ahead of the Spider] MC 900 Ft. Jesus SW1.0 "Short demo tune for Hermit's 2012 tracker, remixing one of my fav rap tunes back in the '90s." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

Indigo [from Rendhagyás EP] RKH GMC1.6 "This is neither a cover, nor a "real" SID tune: it's a work-in-progress demo from the first RKH EP, released in 1995. Finally, this song wasn't included. It has one of the craziest guitar outro riffs I've ever written." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

Inhuman Race [from Brainchain EP] Wackor GMC1.6 "This is neither a cover, nor a "real" SID tune: it's a work-in-progress arrangement demo from the first Wackor EP, released in 1999. The original file had some bugs that were fixed by iAN CooG in 2009." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

It's My Life [from One Love] Dr. Alban GMC1.6 "One of the few covers I created in the early '90s. It had a function back in time. This one was used to create some live arrangement as I did all the song skeletons on C64 for my rock band. During performance we broke stuff and kicked major ass, got banned from clubs and so on. I can recall smashing tellys screaming "no limit" by 2Unlimited playing as a metal song. This actual file rot in the box until C64.sk online cover compo in 2013. May Zombie SIDs never die." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

FC4.0 "Metal SID originally from 1990 or so, inspired by Napalm Death songs. Parts were used in some of my other metal songs during the years. I thought that the disk including that was either lost or damaged but many tunes were returned to me in 2011 that included this workfile. The SIDrip Alliance live set ate all my time so I finalised this one in a few hours before AROK2011 and released the ancient tune there, after more than 20 years passed." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

SW1.9-EMU "My X2026 compotune was originally made for Level 64 demo 'Time Paradox', also released @X'26. As a sort of cinematic leftover of a rather dark demo it may not be an ideal uplifitng compotune but I was happy with it. As opposed to most of my C64 tunes that are riff-driven, this one was built around the drum track that was actually recorded with a drumpad. As most of my SID-Wizard tunes it is a MIDI conversion." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

FC4.0 "Barebone blues trainer from the old times, extraced from a pack of ancient workdisks that was returned to me in May 2011. I used to practice guitar solo improvisation to that. I could not find the title in my archive papers but this trainer loop can be found on a 1990 audio tape containing my earliest tunes so I guess it was among the first SIDs I've ever created." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

GMC1.6 "This tune was the reason for digging out all my old SIDs. I started to make a remix of my LS Tribute in early 2009 but its audio archive was not complete so I had to dig out my old machine. My re-entry to SID composing and demoscene activity started there. Well, I loved Laser Squad so much that I even composed a tribute tune back in 1990-something. This one was among the first tracks I created with GMC 1.6 editor actually. There is also an audio remix of this tune in my 2009 SID remix album, 'rakBIT'." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

GT2.7 "These are 2 short classical guitar trainers I composed back in the early '90s. SIDs were created for SIDwave for the music collection THSX in 2010." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

SW1.4 "It was one of the most challenging tasks I've ever done on many sides. Partly because I had to pack 16 subtunes in $15FF space and partly because I had extremely little time for the project because of album recording project I was working on at the time. So I created all the subtunes with a zero data separator part with a MIDI keyboard and DAW software Reaper as 3-channel MIDI, fed it with SWMconvert.exe and set the sounds. Instead of days the whole project was ready in an afternoon's time, all in all. I had to keep in mind from recordnig the first MIDI note that only a couple of blocks are allowed per subtune because of the memory limit. Due to planning, everything worked fine and it became the most efficient SID project I've done to date." (NP) Title "A MIDI conversion and also a really fast project." (NP) Ingame 01 Ingame 02 Ingame 03 Ingame 04 Ingame 05 Ingame 06 Ingame 07 Ingame 08 Ingame 09 "Crappy Comments" "It uses elements by Rob Hubbard's 'Crazy Comets' but everything is seriously altered of course. I'm not fuckin' Timbaland to directly rip off a SID by someone else in my own production :)" (NP) Ingame 10 "Benn-ifier" "Hermit told me that it has a high dose of Ben Daglish. Somewhat intentional." (NP) Ingame 11 Level start Level complete Lost Game won Highscore NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

Végtelen vidék [from album Sárkányfejezet] Diabolus in Musica SW1.8 "That is where 20 minutes can bring you with SID-Wizard. I wanted to do something for the final round of C64 Grand Tour challenge that no other tracker can do so I recorded a short tune with an Arturia Keylab49 keyboard in Reaper, quantised and arranged channels for a better conversion, exported a 3-channel MIDI file, ran swmconvert.exe on it and set the sounds and some other stuff. The music data is not touched so virtually it is me playing the keyboard. SID-Wizard is a beast of workflow. The title refers to Yennefer from Witcher books, also my childhood as our garden was full of lilac and gooseberries. By today, due to climate change they all gone around my area so that fragrance and memories of the taste also remind me of good people who gone and it completely rips my heart out. After those flashbacks I can't find my way for days. Anyway, this tune is included on Diabouls in Musica LP with lyrics and acoustic guitars. Coupled with deep lyrics I always have to focus to the extreme to not to collapse mentally during live shows when we perform this song called 'Végtelen vidék' or 'Infinite Landscape' as it is about letting it go and saying goodbye forever inevitably." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

MS1.2 "3-sub experimental example tune created for Music Studio 1.2 by Martin Piper." (NP) New Depression Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo) Covers /MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/New_Depression.sid NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

SW1.7 "AC/DC-goes-8-bit-sort-of-SID-tune." (NP) Lumber Lumber "You can sing 'Lumber Lumber' if you wish to." (NP) Angus gone wrong "If you leave worktune fractures in your releases it sounds like that. A sad derivation of the famous AC/DC banger." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

GMC1.6 "My craziest SID tune, ever. This one was in the pack that was given for a demo group called "GMC" for their debut demo called "Brand New". I don't know if they used any of the songs later on but as I can remember they had some problems with the music driver. The tune includes my 02-06-41 horse instrument as mentioned in the 'Moleman 2' 2011 demoscene documentary movie. Everyone believed I was joking with that. I was not." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

M.U.L.E., Tune #1 Roy Glover MS2 "Example tune for MS2, 1-to-1 conversion of the lovely original. Old-school stuff, reminds me of concentrating on melody instead of bells 'n' whistles." (NP). See also /GAMES/M-R/M_U_L_E.sid NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

FC4.0 "Inspired by some movie about the wave of XIX. Century wars of independence I can't rememer the title. Maybe it was 'March into Abyss' or something." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

Mean Streak Matt Gray MS2 "Back in time, we played a lot of this 1987 bikefight game with a goodfellow of mine so the tunes stuck in mind pretty hard. This SID was re-created (and fully remixed in places) with MS2 multi-platform editor by Martin Piper, included as an example tune." (NP). See also /MUSICIANS/G/Gray_Matt/Mean_Streak.sid NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

SID Factory 2 "Megbass is in Hungarian, it means: it fucks you hard. Or something like that. Well, it is not a ballad. The core was created with GoatTracker2 then the music data was imported to SID Factory 2. Easy-peasy. This tracker is very impressive. Perhaps it has the cleanest hard restart I have ever heard. Hi-fi sound fans will love it. I don't know, maybe 8-bit SID chip and hi-fi is a contradiction in terms." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

SW1.2 "It was a test MIDI file that we used to push and test SWMconvert.exe until meltdown as it is a rather irregular piano piece with a lot of data, mixed-up measure and an ample of conversion horror. We could invent many tricks of how to create a MIDI source file for seamless conversion. This experience was super useful for all my later MIDI based SID-Wizard projects. About the creation itself it is basically me playing a MIDI keyboard much slower then the MIDI data is injected directly into SID-Wizard using the SWMconvert.exe tool." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

NT2.03 "API version with 'UFO' style intro. Its original 'home' is an unreleased API demo, a tribure to musician girls. Hence the title, 'Minority Senorita'. Later I added this one to my info PRG file for the C64 executable interactive 'cover' of the SID remix album 'rakBIT' because this one happened to be one of my few tunes that has no SID 8580 vs 6581 issues. I've always had a new 8580 so most probably my instruments sound crap through the more filter-sensitive old 6581 chip. There also exists a 'Rising Sun' version, created for Hokuto Force." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

The Model [from The Man-Machine] Kraftwerk MS1.2 "This one was created with MS1.2 converter from FC4.0 source file. The sounds are tailored to MS. This SID was included in the 1.2 release as an example tune: more powerful sound and fixed bass note." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

The Model [from The Man-Machine] Kraftwerk FC4.0 "My second SID and my last completely finished cover back in the time. For some unknown reason a bass note is out of tune." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

SW1.9-EMU "The the multplatform version of SID-Wizard 1.9 was quite a big thing for me. Before the release I did a lot of testing for Hermit and the result was this tune. I am so honored to be involved in the test team. SW-EMU as we called it, is a beast, the king of workflow. I've been using that since then, almost excusively. About the tune itself, around the covid lockdowns I started to enjoy making these tunes with cleaner orchestration. It is basically a bass synth, a melody line and a drum sequencer. I record these on a synth then convert into a C64 tune with SWMconvert.exe. It adds a little personality to the playing as I play the parts a little different from beat to beat I guess. 3 channels and that's it. Maybe it doesn't sound as heavy as my older stuff where the SID8580 chip wanted to fall apart but still dark as hell, just a different way." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

FC4.0 "This is the last working FC version I could find on a retrieved disk. As far as I can remember, it was the last SID that I created with FC4.0 back in the days. On audio tape labelled 1992 there was an improved version that I re-created in 2010 with Music Studio 1.2 by Martin Piper." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).
MS2 "Converted from MS1.2 and expanded with many new feats of MS2 multiplatform editor. This is the final version." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

MS1.2 "This actual tune was completely re-created from audio archives with Music Studio 1.2 and was included in the release of it as an example/demo tune. This old school-new style editor was fun to use, feels like to be the AC/DC of SID creators :)" (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).
GMC1.6 "One of my heaviest sounding SIDs, based on nifty rock'n'roll riffs. The original file had some bugs that were fixed by iAN CooG in 2009." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

Nautilus, Tune #1 <?> 1RT1.0 "A test tune that uses the very same MIDI source file that I created for my other Nautilus SID. We tested the file converter with it and it passed the test pretty well." (NP) Covers /GAMES/M-R/Nautilus.sid, Tune #1. See also /MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Nautilus_remix.sid NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

Nautilus, Tune #1 <?> SW1.2 "It is a quick MIDI conversion of the old 'Nautilus' game tune for AGod's similar named multiscreen pic. I used SID2MIDI utility that SID remixers use often, I edited the MIDI file a little, exported the SW format then set the sounds. It was ready in an hour or so." (NP) Covers /GAMES/M-R/Nautilus.sid, Tune #1. NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

DMC4.0 "My old SIDding started with FC 4.0 in 1989 and ended with GMC v1.6 in 1994. This is my first tune using something different: DMC was quite a joy to use. Also, was my compo tune for AROK #11 party. The song is based on a metal song of mine from 2004 using heavy riffs. AROK 2009 was an important event for me because that was my 'official' return to the 8-bit scene after 15 years. Among some great guys, I met there with Leon (GFX) and Hermit (coder) who later contributed greatly to my 2009 SID remix album, 'rakBIT'. (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

FC4.0 "That was one of the short intro tunes that I gave to a guy called Aero to use in his stuff during the early '90s. I don't know if he produced anything afterwards. I could not find him in CSDb archives so I guess not." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

GMC1.6 "After releasing 'Flatline' for Didi's cracktro music compo I decided to release a heavier piece, too. It is based on 1994 'Geister' workfiles but I can't recall what was the purpose of the original workfile in the game as there is no any description left." (NP) 1994 workfile from the Geister pack as number $0C NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).
FC4.0 "This short tune included mirroring step bass and melody that I used years later in the Laser Squad Tribute SID." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).
FC4.0 "The first song that was comlpetely written for/with guitar in mind. You would never guess that it's is based on a '70s AC/DC riff." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).
SW1.2 "A little sound effect for Level64 demo intro screens." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).
NT2.03 "Fragment of /MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Ninfa_outro.sid with a tiny intro." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

SW1.2 "A MIDI conversion stitching together 3 different ingame tracks I created for iPhone, most are from Project:Downforce. It was a quick job considering music (melody) data and creating sounds but later on it took a while to sync parts with the flow of the demo. With this SID I used the maximum flexibility of SIDwizard, using the effective MIDI converter, subtune jumper command and all the workflow enhancing and editing functions." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

NT2.03 "The original long version of the main demo tune. The song was originally picked from the hundreds of old demos I've made in MIDI during the years. As the othewise great NinjaTracker has no MIDI converter, just feeding the all the note data was days of work." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).
NT2.03 "A 2:30 cut of the extended version. This is the SID that was finally used in the demo." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

NT2.03 "Inspired by AGod's pictures, this is the 'frame' tune of the demo 'NINFA'. Being groupmates in API, we had nice cooperations so AGod asked me to compose a couple of new tunes for the new L64 demo. I loved their releases and considering the composers like Hein or Intensity (R.I.P.) who had created SIDs for L64 demos - I was honoured." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

GMC1.6 "It was the very first tune that I created for the Ninfa demo but as it turned out the raster hungry GMC driver was not too code friendly so with L64 boys we decided to use more economic drivers, Ninja Tracker and later on SIDwizard. For years it just rested in the box as a worktune but I decided to finish it and release it at Arok 2013." (NP) Won first place at the Arok 2013 music competition. NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

Árnyékod sem... [from Rendhagyás] RKH GMC1.6 "An another arrangement demo song from a 1995 EP that was performed may times by my band. Without lyrics it is a little sleepy but it was an important file to carve the song to its final form back in time." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

FC4.0 "It is a guitar solo trainer from my early guitar player days. It was my first song-like full tune I guess, with the footnote that it lacks arrangement as such..." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

NT2.03 "A NinjaTracker tune must include some ninja weapon as we concluded with Vincenzo thinking about the title of the C64GTC NinjaTracker round. He created Part1 and I did Part2, trying to capture the feel of a ninja karate kung-fu hero movie or game. Maybe it is too porn for that. You decide." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).
FC4.0 "A Ben Daglish-inspired fast tune, featuring one of my first guitar solo ideas that I converted to C64." (NP) NecroPolo's own comments are denoted (NP).

GMC1.6 "Prolyx-69 was a two-member demo group who asked me to write some songs for their stuff. They had some extreme sense of humour that today would be sexist. These guys now would end up in a court saying things that was absolutely harmless back in the days. Now'days it would have been offensive and they would have been sued by a dosen of feminist activists I guess. I don't know anything about them. Maybe they are in jail, who knows. They were called Devo and Robbo. Great guys. Anyway, while this tune was finished, the demo that was a hilarious pussy licking tutorial actually, was unfortunately not. SW1.8 "An another production-time-efficient SID-Wizard MIDI conversion of mine, created for disgmag Propaganda no.31. "Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. Sascha and I made it a night. Sleep, what's that? By that time, I had figured out what number to add to the filter byte to get roughly the same sound as with normal filters." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. One of my longest tunes -- and one of my best! The first part is partly inspired by J.S.Bach and Jeroen Tel, the second part mostly by Drax, being rather short (out of inspiration, just up'n'down the blues scale). Uptonogood (don't remember the group, sorry) from Australia used this music in his mag 'The Link'." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. Inspired by J.S.Bach again, I composed this piece as another magsound for 'Genetic Dreams' by Trinomic Boozeline. Willy/Presence favored this piece a lot (he himself liking Bach, too). I chose the name with a sidelook to Sascha's piece 'Drax' Domain'. This piece consists of a few different parts which I just lined up one after another, as I was unable to come up with some interludes." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

Main Title [from the movie Back to the Future Part III] Alan Silvestri "Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster. This is a remake of the title tune from the game. Hawk had asked me to do it." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. I wrote this piece to express my feelings about a freshly broken relationship with my (former, sigh) girlfriend. As we just had analyzed fugues in music class, I wrote a fugue (in c-minor) as well. There is a zeropage version of this tune that saves even more rastertime and memory." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"This tunes had been composed with the full player in mind (an loaded into the editor). That player uses a slight de-tuning for voice #2 and #3 in order to achieve a fuller sound. In addition, the instruments make use of pulse width modification. For the 'zero page version' of this piece, I had cut down the player to almost nothing in order to get a real short file with as little raster time as possible. During that step, I removed the routine for the pulse modification and increased the detuning of voice #2 and #3 instead, resulting in a slightly different (and slightly less nice) sound." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with Chris Hülsbeck's Soundmonitor. What a shame that I couldn't make a real FAT bassdrum!" (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. I originally had planned to write a techno tune (without too much success, as you can hear). It's one of my personal favorites." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster. A magsound for the Alcoholics. I don't know if they actually used it." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. Out of inspiration for any new music, I was listening to some of my old tunes and started to play around with the old 'Groovy Night'. The result was this funny little thing. Listen to the portamento with the arpeggio (the drop-down)!" (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster. In the big band I played the trumpet in at that time, we used to play 'Cowboy Song' by Fred Lipsius. I couldn't exactly play it properly, but I like it very much nevertheless. So I took its name for this tune (which is the only thing these two pieces have in common)." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. A funny thing for Trance's diskmag 'A-Head', inspired by the music to 'Moons' by Drax." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with Chris Hülsbeck's Soundmonitor. Again a tune my trumpet teacher liked a lot! This tune was publically performed (err... played from tape) at a performance of his trumpet class I was a pupil in. I was very proud of the drums I had squeezed out of little Soundmonitor." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

Eternal Sadness Traditional "Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster. A schoolmate had asked me to arrange this traditional funeral march for him. I did my best, but in the end he didn't really like the result he came to hear. =:-(" (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with Chris Hülsbeck's Soundmonitor. I wrote this tune and the previous one on the same afternoon in order to impress a girl from dancing class (without success, alas). But at least it was fun discussing politics with her on the phone." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

Happy Birthday Mildred J. Hill "Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. Just a another crappy conversion of this traditional birthday song. Too many wrong chords." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with Chris Hülsbeck's Soundmonitor. A play on words with the German word for Corpus Christi Day ('Fronleichnam')." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!." (OK) "This swingy thing was composed for the Jump'n'Run 'Henry' by Peter Schwarzfischer (Sky/Masters' Design Group). My first Swing tune for a long time (since the 'Underground-Rock'). As it seems, I will still compose a different piece for Level 1, as the game has changed its mood from funny to more Fantasy-like and gloomy. This music is rather old anyway." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

Lenor advert theme <?> "Done with Future Composer II. I didn't like this editor at all (and didn't understand it in full, either). An acquaintance from the scene (Doc Holliday or someone from Presence ) asked me to convert this music from the 'Lenor' TV ad to C64." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with Chris Hülsbeck's Soundmonitor." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. Inspired by some tune by Laxity (and with some of its instruments, ripped by hand). In English, the 'Lax' Up' is pronounced exactly the same as the German translation of 'lick it off' (leck's ab). =:-> " (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster. Hawk/Presence once asked me to compose a short tune for a loader. As far as I know, this music has never been used with a loader, though." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with my first own music player. Having read about the great features of Soundmonitor, I got fed up with the limits of The Music System (TMS) and the music commands from BASIC V7.0. So I wrote my own soundplayer. That thing ate memory and rastertime like I drink tea and used a notation similar to the BASIC commands. But -- it worked and had cool *filters*! I planned to use it in a Snake-like game I was coding (Crowding Crawlers), but the game made heavy use of raster interrupts and color effects and thus would not work with the music (rastertime ranging from $03 to $80 or so...). I never finished the game anyway. But my trumpet teacher liked the tune _very_ much! =:-> " (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with Oliver Blasnik's Romuzak." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

Piano Sonata in C (KV 545) (0:00-0:06) Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart "Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. A 4-time techno tune (my best one of this kind so far) which I wrote together with a good friend of mine, Ingo Meyer. While we were composing, the speaker box fell off the shelf due to one extremely loud bass-kick (no kidding!). This piece contributed to the music competition at the Data-Live '93 in Dessau, winning the 2nd place. Possibly it would have made the 1st if they had had good big speakers instead of that tiny thing in their video beamer! =:-( " (OK) Also used in the game "Orb", (C) 1994 Magic Disk 64/CP Verlag. Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with Oliver Blasnik's Romuzak. I came up with the name as my mother didn't like the sound of the arpeggios at all." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

Sascha/DOS/MDG liked this tune very much and said to me, grinning: 'I think you've listened to Maniacs of Noise far too much!'" (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster. What a horror: I couldn't think of any sensible name for this piece of music!" (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with Oliver Blasnik's Romuzak. I wrote this tune and the previous one for Presence, both on the same weekend (I obviously felt that I had to become a little more active)." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with Oliver Blasnik's Romuzak. A guy from Red Sector Inc. asked me to compose a lame-sounding cool tune (whatever he might exactly have thought of) for an intro of their second group, Ultimate (the section for crap releases)." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).
"Done with Chris Hülsbeck's Soundmonitor." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with Chris Hülsbeck's Soundmonitor. Again a (rather obvious) play on words. At that time, I used to write either Rock'n'Roll style tunes or the usual 'cool' style SID-tunes with mainly minor scales." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. This piece was composed at the Data Live '93 for the party report by TRL Designs ('The Real Lunatic'). I had a very nasty back-ache after the piece was finished." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster. I composed this piece at the Security group Meeting in December 1991 in Mannheim. Security (Demons of Sound [DOS] being part of it) was my second group at that time. With this tune, I started a new approach to composing on the C64, very much Vibrants-like: start with a groovy bassline and write the lead voice last, using a lot of blues scale." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. I wrote this piece for Galen/Trinomic (Trinomic Boozeline) for his mag 'Genetic Dreams' (my favorite mag) as an apology: I had promised to do a few conversions for their demo but didn't get them finished in time. So they had to use non-exclusive music." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with SoedeSoft's SoundMaster. This name was supposed to sound Hungarian. My trumpet teacher (who is Hungarian) knew better, though. But he liked that tune a lot. I composed it for Asterix/Victory as a music for his diskmag." (OK) Odi's (Oliver Klee) own comments are denoted (OK).

"Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!. My first finished attempt to write some techno. entries.s: "This tune marks the beginning of a new era of my personal development as a musician. Until then I had only desperately struggled to get familiar with the Sound Monitor and its features, and now I actually started USING them. Originally I only gave the tunes numbers instead of names, but now, about 20 years later, I felt like it was time to also add some names." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"Unlike many other of my songs until this point, I had composed and arranged this tune on my Casio keyboard BEFORE I started working on the SID. I'm not 100% content with the arpeggios, but it's Ok, I'm proud of this SID. Interlude (1:46-2:04) inspired by Tanita Tikaram's Twist in My Sobriety." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
Spacelab [from The Man-Machine] (0:00-2:30) Kraftwerk Cybernoid, Tune #1 (2:31-4:28) Jeroen Tel Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

Carbonara (3:09-4:54) Spliff "I ran out of ideas for the first part, so I added the second, bouncy part just for fun. But I like the first part better. I should have let this tune end at 3:08." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
Thundercats Rob Hubbard Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"This tune's supposed to be the successor of my -3, but I'm very discontent with it. Especially the fast part starting at 3:59 is uninspired and sort of ridiculous. Lead sound starting at 3:43 inspired by Chris Grigg's Maniac Mansion and Matthew Kane's Zak McKracken." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"I was (and still am) very proud of this tune. At that time, it was my best one so far, at least IMHO. Especially the no-melody part (1:23-1:52) is very crisp and drummy. Bass starting at 2:54 inspired (once again) by Jeroen Tel's Cybernoid." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
Mirror of Soul Peter Thierolf Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Bouncy and a little thin-sounding. Not bad, but nothing special!" (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
Inspired by LED Storm on the Amiga. (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"I consider this tune my final breakthrough to the world of good SID music. The sound is the best I could squeeze out of the Sound Monitor. Rocks! Only the filtered lead sound at 1:31 doesn't sound in Sidplay as it's supposed to." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Slightly influenced by Martin Galway's Arkanoid." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"After I had been very content with the tune -19, I lost my orientation a little. I wanted to try something new, but it became too bouncy and light-weight, not the way I wanted it to sound like." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"After I had been very content with the tune -19, I lost my orientation a little. I wanted to try something new, but it became too bouncy and light-weight, not the way I wanted it to sound like." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

Cybernoid II, Tune #1 Jeroen Tel "This tune represents everything I had been trying to achieve since tune -1. This is the tune from that period I'm most proud of." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"Only slightly inspired by Martin Galway's Yie-Ar Kung Fu. With this tune I tried to create another masterpiece like tune -22, but unfortunately it kind of went over the top somehow. Especially the grave part starting at 3:09 isn't as powerful as I wanted it to be." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
The Dungeons [from the C64 game The Last Ninja] Anthony Lees "Also slightly influenced by Martin Galway's Arkanoid." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Bass inspired by Martin Galway's Combat School title tune." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

Central Park (loader) [from the C64 game Last Ninja 2] (0:00-4:01) Matt Gray Parallax, Tune #1 (4:02-6:53) Martin Galway "The snaredrum was added later. With this tune I fooled a friend, telling him that I had finished playing Last Ninja 2 (while we were still both stuck in level 3) and that I was able to load the outro tune in Sound Monitor. He believed me. ;-) This is my earliest tune I'm really proud of." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"After I was so proud of tune -5, I felt a little burnt out and became uninspired in -6 to -9." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
Girl You Know It's True (0:00-2:54) Milli Vanilli Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

Doctor in the Tardis (2:18-3:25) The Timelords (KLF) Equinoxe Part 4 [from Equinoxe] (3:26-6:23) Jean-Michel Jarre "My first (uninspired) tune with this cool snaredrum. I had found it in some demo tune, which I got by incident after I had already given up hope to ever find a good snaredrum in Sound Monitor. In the Jarre part, I rhythmically got something wrong, I know." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Uninspired strumming, just to tryout my new snare drum sound." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Short but bad! Inspired by Parker's Amidar video game." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"This tune paints the flight of an Air Force jet, with start, flight (with stormy weather and clouds inbetween), and finally the landing. Lead sound starting at 1:54 inspired by Fred Gray's Mutants. Some of the arpeggios and noise waveforms inspired by Martin Walker's Armalyte." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"This is the SID I'm most proud of. The tune was also recorded later as "Patty, Kim & Gunnar" with keyboards and vocals and had the title "Just Good Friends". It was "covered" in 1996 by Dieter Bohlen, who we had sent a demo tape to, and released in 1996 as Blue System's single "Only With You" and on his album "Body To Body". Of course I was neither asked for permission nor given a profit sharing. The single went #58 on the German charts." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"I wrote this as a love song for a girl named Kim, at least I thought so. She of course never listened to it, as she didn't want to have anything to do with a freaky C64 nerd like me. Weeks later I found out that the girl's name wasn't Kim at all, but I didn't change the title of this tune to her real name. Mind the funny ping-pong sound starting at 3:09! ;-)" (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Just a small sound study." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"With this elaborate composition, I ran out of memory very quickly. At 1:41-1:45 I frivolously used a "forbidden" memory part, so the music data is overwritten during the initialization of the tune's playback by the drums samples. Bummer! Tune inspired by Rondo Veneziano." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"The samples sound quite muddy in this one, probably bc the filter in the bass sound interferes with them. Bummer!" (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"My first tune with digidrums, which I had ripped from the game "Danger Freak". This tune marks a turning-point in my personal development as a musician, putting the focus more on harmonies and elaborate arpeggios than trying to produce a "cool sound". From this tune on, I also made myself a strict rule that I FIRST finish composing the tune on my piano or my Casio keyboard and THEN switch the C128 on and start with the data input. In order to reflect this, I also started to give the tunes names instead of numbers again." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Inspired by the 1986 Sylvester Stallone movie." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Another prototype for a song I wanted to record later with electric guitar, keyboard and vocals, which then, as always, never happened." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Refrain starting at 1:16 inspired by Vangelis' Bladerunner OST." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"Just a prototype for a song I wanted to record later with a couple of friends using keyboards, electric guitar and vocals. But that never happened. ;-)" (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"My very first composition on the piano. I made it as a kid, long before I started making SID music." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"Just some uninspired strumming recorded "live" without any quantization. Horrible! Skip this one!!! ;-)" (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

Stormlord intro Jeroen Tel "I had originally intended to add digidrums to this one, but after finishing the 3 "regular" voices I had already used up too much memory. So I just left the tune as it was." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"This tune's title was actually the name of a character from a radio comedy show called "FFN Frühstyxradio", Suzette Nietmeyer, spoken by Sabine Bulthaup. http://www.fruehstyxradio.de/ " (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).
"In this tune I tried to musically describe what it looks like in the mind of a madman." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"My very first SID tune ever. It was made while I read the Sound Monitor tutorial in a C64 magazine. Everything mentioned there went into this tune, step by step. Unfortunately, quantization was not mentioned there, as you can hear in the improvisational part starting at 2:41. ;-) Bass inspired by Erasure's Ship Of Fools." (KH) Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"This is my first SID I actually consider a real composition. I was very proud of this one back then." (KH) ### /MUSICIANS/O/Onebitman/ ################################################## Kim Homann's own comments are denoted (KH).

"In July 2015, I had surgery, which resulted me in being off work for about 3 months. So, I had some time spare! So, I started writing SID music again for fun. My first release (FIRST) is very much a 'standard' SID. It has the same instruments and structure as I was writing and hearing in 1990." (JP) Jason Page's own comments are denoted (JP).

"I decided that if I could make the percussion sounds more 'realistic', then I'd effectively have a synth and a drum machine. For too long, people seem to have used the same techniques for creating percussion sounds (since Maniacs of Noise...). I think that a lot of people stopped pushing the SID, and the music (although great) seemed to be stuck in a rut. I knew FORTH was on the right track, as some people thought it was fake (using samples / multiple SID's) which made me happy! It was here that I also tested my theories for some of my percussion sounds. The hi hats and clap sounds were what I hoped would raise my SID's to a new level. The hi hats especially, as these really changed the overall sound of the SID. Most SID's don't have those high frequencies. And the clap, it sounded like a real drum machine. So again, helped change the perceptions of a lot of listeners regarding the pushing of SID boundaries." (JP) Jason Page's own comments are denoted (JP).

Thalamusik [from the game Sanxion] Rob Hubbard "This was another experiment, where I wanted to see if I could remix an existing (and brilliant) SID tune, but only using a SID. I've heard (and made) a number of remixes on Remix64, but wanted to attempt to do the same and hopefully be better than a lot of those, but with nothing but a SID. This was far more difficult to do than Turrican! I initially converted the whole of Sanxion to SidTracker64. So, all of the patterns and instruments. So at this point, I had a version of the track that ran on ST64 in 4x speed (something I've been doing since Forth. It's how I can get the definition on the clap and snare...). Only at that point could I start remixing. I didn't want to completely destroy the feeling of the original, but I wanted to change it enough to make it worthwhile remixing. It was difficult to gauge what I could do to keep that balance. Also, the whole track is basically based around ringmod and sync instruments. What this means is that the sound of, say, the lead instrument, is effected by another instrument. So, if I modify one instrument for the remix, it could easily mess up another completely. Likewise, even when porting to ST64, if an instrument wasn't created exactly as the original, or if I used the wrong note, it could make the whole thing sound wrong. But, it seems that a lot of people like the result. I knew it would be down to personal taste, as the original track is so iconic. I knew some just wouldn't like it. I can live with that." (JP) Jason Page's own comments are denoted (JP).

Turrican intro music [from the Amiga game] Chris Hülsbeck "For Hybris (which I released before Turrican), I worked out how to reduce channels but keep the quality. So, I kind of knew that I could get the Amiga's 4 channels down to 3 for Turrican. My main goal here was to write a track that didn't use ARP's (those instruments where it quickly changes between notes to create a chord effect). The Amiga version didn't use them, and I felt that if I had to resort to using them in the port, then I would have failed. It would have just sounded like a C64 version of an Amiga track. I wanted it to sound just like the Amiga track, if not better! It only took 2 days or so to write. The main problem was trying to get the chords to work, without them cutting out the melody line and so on. It all comes down to basically tricking the listener. I could remove one voice for another, and as long as it wasn't *that* noticeable, I could get away with it. Kind of similar to how MP3's work, by only storing the information that the user can hear, I guess." (JP) ### /MUSICIANS/P/Pajda ####################################################### Jason Page's own comments are denoted (JP).

entries.s: Hymn to Aurora [from the Amiga MOD module] Horace Wimp "The first version I made on my Atari a few years ago and since I love this MOD, I also had to make the C64 version. I was trying to make the instruments sound the nearest possible to the original and I was quite successful (also because I ripped the trumpet sound from some DOS/ADSR tune - check /MUSICIANS/D/DOS/Pursuit.sid). Sounds best on a real C64." (ZE) All comments on PseudoGrafx's tunes are by the author Zdenek Eisenhammer (ZE).

Close to Me [from The Head on the Door] The Cure "This is probably my last tune ever made on C64 - finished in March 97. I really wonder why I did it in TFX 1.3 although v2.4 was already finished..." (ZE) All comments on PseudoGrafx's tunes are by the author Zdenek Eisenhammer (ZE).

Laser Squadron [from the Atari XL/XE game] Dieter Bohlen "A cover of an ATARI XL/XE music from an ugly german game, which was really lame although it was quite new ('92 or '93). The music was cool anyway :-)." (ZE) All comments on PseudoGrafx's tunes are by the author Zdenek Eisenhammer (ZE).

"Made for the font collection in Unreal's tooldisk 'Tooltime'. My first original tune (not a cover) on C64 (November 95). Tooltime was full of this tune - it was used in nearly all notes on the disk because we didn't have any other tunes to use and we didn't want to use the ripped ones." (ZE) All comments on PseudoGrafx's tunes are by the author Zdenek Eisenhammer (ZE).

Mountain Bike Racer, Tune #1 Adam Gilmore This was my first C64 tune made in October 95 and also the first tune ever finished in our music editor TFX 1.0. It covers ATARI XL/XE version, since I had an 800XE before C64. Anyway the C64 version is nearly the same. Maybe if I had known that Adam Gilmore made it also on C64, I wouldn't have covered it." (ZE) All comments on PseudoGrafx's tunes are by the author Zdenek Eisenhammer (ZE).

"IMHO my worst tune because I was absolutely out of inspiration when doing it. I had to finish it during one afternoon since it was a tune for our partyreport which was held on one weekend in spring 96 - and I also had to make a picture for that report on the same day. My first tune made in an improved version of TFX - v1.3." (ZE) All comments on PseudoGrafx's tunes are by the author Zdenek Eisenhammer (ZE).

Wish Me Luck [from the Amiga MOD module] Martin Wall (Mantronix) Made for Ray's (Unreal's main coder and HQ) request. It was quite an easy work to rewrite it (he recorded the module for me on a tape since I didn't have PC yet) - it took me only 1 day and it's nearly the same as the original. Made in February 1997. Sounds the best on a real C64." (ZE) ### /MUSICIANS/P/Psych858o ################################################### All comments on PseudoGrafx's tunes are by the author Zdenek Eisenhammer (ZE).

"This was done very quick & dirty, if I remember right I've had only 3-4 hours time to compose this track in our new developed and finished Reflex-Tracker, a 2 channel sampletracker. Access Denied sample spoken by me. The bass-drumm split was make with an Amiga 500 and converted to my C64. Later in version v1.1 of Reflex-Tracker the user could do this without directly in the trakker. Funny: most of the time in this song I use only one digichannel, after release I created a remix which prooves the ability of Reflex-Tracker a little bit better. After winning the C64 democompo at THE PARTY'94 in Denmark, most of the people thought our group name is 'Access Denied' but it was 'Reflex' instead ;)" (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"This is the remix of Access_Denied_intro.sid where I show some of the features of Reflex-Tracker: 2 channels of digi-sounds, faked third voice (drum and snare which are rendered in the bassvoice), volume, echoeffects and flanger. All samples by me, except the "ho ho" which I have sampled from the german rap song 'Edelweiß'." (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"Interesting fact: it's a 2 channel digi music but not a Reflex-Tracker tune. It's a routine which allows you theoretical add 3 SID voices. The music editor is named 'Perfect Sound 3.2'. Unfortunately the 2 digi voices have always the speed (and pitch) of the first digi voice and if you really use both voices the SID channels were nearly destroyed and the CPU was down... We used this track in the note file of our (Reflex) first trackmo 'Cafe Odd'. Later it became a very nice practice for us to use always a very special notefile-soundroutine for our trackmos. All (!) samples was sampled with my Phillips-Workman!! Sample-software by Zork and TTS! Sampler by Zork's Brother." (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

Axel F [from the movie Beverly Hills Cop] Harold Faltermeyer "My second doublespeed tune. After all the other conversions of this great song I thought it was a good idea not only to use the original melody. The great mood with the sfx and sounds should even be copied. At 2:01 I started to remix the song with some special drums and clave sticks." (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".
PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".
PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"If you are using a old SID chip or emulation you will probably not hear too much from the melody line, the 6581 doesn't know the used $31 waveform. Sorry for that. Doesn't know much about this song, its 15 years ago and this song was only made just 4 fun and to learn... I never planned to release this song (and during composing this I even didn't have the ability to do this^^)" (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

px.bladeswede remix! [from the Amiga game Project-X] Allister Brimble "I listened to Allister Brimble's great song on Amiga and decided that this song has to be remixed to the C64. Unfortunately I don't have the needed amount of channels so I used a big bunch of arpeggio-lead & bass-splits. The patterns looks like a exploded memorydump, it was very hard to compose this with a durationeditor (DMC4.x). I really forced the lead melody between the arpeggios. The music got used in Access Denied trackmo-notefile with a raytraced animation and a layered scroller. Regarding our tradition to use some special in our trackmo-notefiles I tried a faked 4 speed tune, that means: normal doublespeed routine and additionally I called the sidroutine 2 times (without the filterroutine), that gives: 4speed wave and 2speed filter." (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".
PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".
PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"Again a Reflex-Tracker song, the rap and the beats are realtime mixed. Rapped by myself ;) The string was ripped from Georg Brandt's Paranoia_Complex.sid, Tune #1, thanks to Georg! As I've made this tune I thought it would be a revolution, the first realtime rap on C64 and so... but no one, I repeat: no one! cared about ;) Later I composed a very long CBA&Nightshade hate hip-hop track, (they have stolen and cracked a game which we have made), but this song was never spread by our swapper Happymaker. Very sad.)" (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"This is one of the few songs which I have made in our own SID-editor called LSD (Low Sound Dealer, IIRC). Nothing special here, I think I have composed this tune mustly to show what clear filter sounds are possible with this routine. It's a single speeder. Unfortunately I didn't know the trackmo (Breitbandkatze / Reflex) and the demo parts during composing. You need a new SID chip, or you will miss some complete channels. It's possible that this tune is the track, which I would do just for fun with the goal that no voices are listenable on a old SID chip. But I'm not sure if I realy have done this, its not very hard to do such things ;) (my intention: all my filtereffects sounds horrible on a old SID and I thought it was better to show listeners with old SID nothing than crap) it was the last song which I did on C64 after 5 years of SID composing. Since 2001 and now (2008) I rarely compose SID tunes with QuadraSID, one or two times per year. Some of this tracks you can download from my website as mp3 (www.reflex-studio.com)" (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"This is the first music which was done in the Reflex-Tracker engine, without editor. 8) I "composed" this track live at THE PARTY'93 in Denmark, in assembler... I typed the pattern and notes with Action Replay monitor in the memory. It was a very funny time, with hardcore party in the sleeping hall and so on 8)" (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"The first trackmo of our group Reflex which was released at THE PARTY '93. The first trackmo with a doublespeed music 8) This was the first music of me on C64 which was really released AND spreaded ;) This trackmo also have two 2 channel digiparts! The first one is in the notefile, listen to Africa_Corps.sid and read the STIL comments! The second one is the first version of our 2 years later released Reflex-Tracker. The Cafe_Odd_end.sid digi music was composed in pure assembler." (PVCF) 6581 version. 8580 version. PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"The SID music and the digisequence was composed with two different routines: 3sid voices in DMC4.x and after finishing I have loaded it in Polonus' DigiTracker and added the samplesequences. Very funny way to compose: if you changed a sample, for example after 2 min in songlength, you have to start the song from begin to check if it works in minute two. I was very masochistic those days. Polonus did NOT include a fast forward routine, so later I added one in his editor." (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"The trackmo Centric/Reflex of our gamesection 'Cyance' won a C64/Amiga democompetition at a multiplatform party in Berlin in 1996, IIRC. We decided to give up the trackmo spontaneously, but it was a big success :) To tell the truth: I don't like this song very much, especially the total uninspired first minute is horrible. It's a doublespeed song. This is one of the few songs which I have made in our own SID-editor called LSD (Low Sound Dealer, IIRC)." (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"I've spent very long time for the whole project, I think something about 6-9 months (besides graduation diploma and some rfx-trackmos). as the game was finished and the music was put in and I played it, I noticed: "shit, I've made the first ingame musics very very long, 2-5 minutes each and the players died after some seconds of playing!" That was a very harsh lesson. Oh, and the game sold horrible... Later I composed most of the following songs a little bit shorter." (PVCF) "This is one of the few songs which I have made in our own SID-editor called LSD (Low Sound Dealer, IIRC)." (PVCF) "This was the menu tune" (PVCF) "Loader tune" (PVCF) "ingame1, huh, about every 30 seconds a totally different style." (PVCF) "ingame2, if you like techno on C64 this song is possible for you" (PVCF) "nice ringmodulation at the beginning, it was only a loader tune." (PVCF) Danger Freak, Tune #1 Chris Hülsbeck "ingame3, I tried to copy the original melody and soundset from 'Danger Freak/Chris Hülsbeck'. Just 4 fun :)" (PVCF) "ingame4, too long, too many styles, too much work..." (PVCF) "Only a loadertune" (PVCF) "ingame5, a multispeed song, the original title is 'dance of the robot', one of my favourite songs :)" (PVCF) Scapelands Kai Walter (PVCF) "ingame6, a very nice remix of Scapelands.sid, just after the first 30 seconds of boreness, which was released in Access Denied trackmo. I also put in some Martin Galway like athmosphere, listen from 1:30 for this." (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".
PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

Look Who's Talking [from Look Who's Talking] Dr. Alban "Yeah, a 5-speed tune, IIRC. The drumtable was longer than my arm ;) Just composed for fun. it sounds a little disharmonic at begin, that's caused by Brian/Graffity, who didn't implement the right frequency table in his DMCs. From DMC4 I used a own table, which KB/TOM/farbrausch has edited. From 2:30 min there are very nice remixes and soundeffects which are inspired by the samples from Bad Cat by Chris Hülsbeck 8)" (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"This song was composed live on a local computerparty. I would say it was funny, but on other had: how funny is a party where you sit down and work on a C64 and there is only one of this machine running and other people (Ron Grahnert aka Odysseus) are even bored and tried to get his hands on the keyboard? So we found a compromise and worked 10 min each on DMC :) That's the result! Ah, one interesting thing: it's a special more and halfspeed-mix. "Very funny story why I created this song: if you look carefully in this directory you will find a song called "Axel_F" which I adapted from Harold Faltermeyer. I found out, if I play the original Beverly Hills Cop chords from Axel F in the other direction OR simultaneously it's exact(!) the same like "The Great Giana Sisters, Tune #5". To answer all other game related questions: NO! :) It was NOT a Giana/Mario-clone. It was NOT released. I have NO copy (only one level was finished and playable, ask Quiss!) We do NOT have had a permission to use the name and the sprites of Giana :) The idea: what do if you get stressed by work / family / girlfriend/... ? What about a game where you can shoot very brutal? What enemy would you like to kill to vent your anger? Right! The dinky Giana Sister :p And what weapon would you like to use to kill Giana? Right! A tank! So here is the game: you have a tank with a machinegun which drove from right to left (on your will) and from above it was raining little Giana Sisters with parachutes. Now you could use your heavy machinegun and blow them into hell (subtune #6!). If you missed one and landed in front of you, you could try to drive with your tank chain over Giana :) then #5 was played. If you only have destroyed the parachute and little Giana falls & hit the ground #4 was played. #7 if a Giana hits your tank (and eats some of your health)." "This is one of the few songs which I have made in our own SID-editor called LSD (Low Sound Dealer, IIRC). One of my costly and longest LSD tracks. in this routine I could trigger demoparts with numeric commands in the soundpattern, Quiss (the programmer of LSD and some of the trackmoparts in Mathematica) have included a fallback routine in the demo, that waits 10 sec if the floppydrive of the user is to slow and a trigger was missed. Unfortunately he forgot to tell me that the first numeric trigger he was expecting was a "0". But I began the count with "1" ... so 10 sec failbackpause is in all versions of mathematica, right before the Doom-part. Funny thing: exact 5.34 min long was the centerpart, I composed exact 5.34 min :) but I don't know about the 10 sec fall back routine, and Quiss didn't tell me... he simply took notice that the music was too "short", removed the stop-bytes at the end of the LSD track and was satisfied. Watching the trackmo first time and live at THE PARTY'95 I was pissed of as I saw/heard the result: the music wild remixed itself after 5.34 unless the last part was finished. I learned one thing: (its true up to now, 2008!!) programmers don't have any savvy about music. Last funny thing: I asked all people around me what they thought about this crazy and disharmonic music? All(!) comments sounded like this: "If PVCF compose like this it has to be like this" ... aha.. ha ..ha... Funny thing: after the democompetition the organizers have shown this trackmo again, in this time (1995) Mathematica was like a revolution on C64 in design & code and I put in at 1:36 a little irish sounding melody which forced some people with hooked arms to dance together on tables, I was very very very proud :p It's possible that you need a new SID chip to hear this part, sorry for that. (yes, the trackmo has a SID chip-selector and detector, but this should be used in an other trackmo of us, read the STIL comments for Mathematica_tune_1_6581.sid for more informati

"Uhh, this song taught me a very hard lesson: save your work every 3-5 minutes, ... save !!!! I worked on Megasweet a whole day and I swear, it was twice as good as what you can hear now. But after about 8 hours of composing on my C64 (it was a sunny day, I ought to learn for my A-level examination) the C64 was freezed (a DMC-crash which occured about once per year). After that I was so frustrated that I released this truly unfinished version. Check out the great mp3 conversion from DJ SKITZ. To be honest I have ripped out the idea for the filtered glide effect in the main bassline from an Amiga-mod called "Megasweet". I thought it would be nice to try something similar on C64 for testing purpose. Then I added the chord, but didn't play it as arpeggio-sound (typical C64), instead I played it like a triad, very slow and voila - the base idea of the first real trance/chill techno music on C64 was born. Now the "work" begun: in DMC4 doesn't exists a filtercommand in pattern, so I must use different filtered basses and endless glide-effects in bassline. It's not much fun to work like this." (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"This was made for and released in the trackmo 'Radio Napalm' of our group 'Reflex', which has won a party, but I can't remember which. [It won the X'95 demo competition held in Utrecht, Netherlands] Quiss told me it was shown with a old SID chip 6581 and the music wasn't that what it should be supposed to, but the crowd was so impressed by the trackmo that the applause during the whole demo was even louder than the sound equipement. So the old SID wasn't that much of a problem :) It's a DMC music and I hate it for the 16 slots instrument limitation, you can hear it: the filter doesn't sweep smooth at the first part, they are like triggered in a mod file. :( Later I released this song in one of our Brainbeat music collections, but I forgot to relocate the song, so every one could load the tune directly in his DMC. The result: some very bad remixes (which uses this horrible filter off-set soundsystem). The party [the demo was released on] had a limitation in length of demos: 5 minutes. So first I composed the music as a 5 minutes track. Unfortunately Quiss (the coder of the trackmo) didn't get enough parts in time to fill up the 5 minutes complete. We first have planned to show during the whole demo a backward timer which runs from 5 min to 0 with the comment "We hate timelimits!!!". After Quiss told me the lack of a needed last part I shortened the music drastically. I have done this track on a new SID chip, KB/TOM (now farbrausch) later converted this song for the old SID chip and released a "old SID chip" version of the trackmo." (PVCF) PVCF is short for "Pro Velochistische Contra Fraction".

"That's exactly what my emotions were as I used this tune in my last demo, on the last screen. It was the Dexion-party in 1988. I had released 'Apolloguys' the same day, and I had bought my Amiga 500 only 2 weeks before coming to this party. The first screen featured 'Like Galway', and me writing a lot of text about who and what 'Rambones' was. The middle screen was the 'Amiga Noid' screen, with a small picture of an Amiga, and a scroll telling that TST would soon rule it. The last one, with this music, was a 10 point list of things about the C64 that bored the hell out of me. Things like colorbars, sprites moving in sinus, Hubbard alike drums/routines, all with the same sound and generally everything that was in at that time. For me it was sad to see a large variety of composers using more or less the same routine, leaving the music in a grey state. I admire the sound of Fred Gray, Martin Galway, Rob Hubbard, David Whittaker, Ben Daglish and Antony Crowther, and any other programmer that built it all up from scratch." "This needs filter! (C64)... As I saw that Jonathan Dunn continued to make music for Ocean, I thought that maybe I had a chance also, so I sent this tune to the company. I never got a reply. :) well, I didn't really care anyway because I now was using Soundtracker every day, all day long. My newfound inspiration: SLL .. :) After having made my first few Soundtracker-modules, I sent a demo with some musics and a picture to Hewson. They replied: your music is quite good, but we cannot accept you as a graphics-artist, the picture lacks all kind of inspiration. Arrrghh.... Their music in their games sucked bigtime back then... This is the last tune that I made in 1988." (JH) Jan Harries own comments are denoted (JH). "The 80's tunes here, are made in 1986-1988, with Soundmonitor and Rockmonitor 3. The 90's and 2000's tunes are made with JCH's editor, and SID Duzz It" (JH)

"Everybody old enough knows the 'Ode To Martin' by MC/Dutch USA-Team. One of my good contacts, and a very musical one to was Banana/The Electronic Knights. He had already made more than 30 tunes when I first laid my hands on Soundmon. I didn't know at all how to use this program, but I could hear from Chris' and Banana's music that it definately was the way to go. So I asked Banana for some help. He sent me about 10 handwritten pages, how to type in this bass and use the program. So, it was my FIRST tune ever!" (JH) Jan Harries own comments are denoted (JH). "We are in the final chapter of my C64 days. I was composing / drawing / programming / writing, all alone on my final demo: Zound Muzak #4. I had just learned FLD, 8-9 months after everybody else, but at least I didn't just rip it. I started on several tunes at the same time, to try and get them all to sound as they came from one whole, like Mike Oldfield does. This was the first one, but I never finished ZM4, I was too bored after all." (JH) Revolution Previously this tune was only playing a subset of the whole song, the final version was forgotten and found out in 2023 after 35 years. "This tune does exactly what it says on the box, basically trying to get a ring-mod effect that sounded like an electric guitar being left leaning on a Marshall amplifier turned up to 11. I was fairly pleased with the result, it sounds quite uncomfortable on headphones. The tune was written on a SoedeSoft editor, which explains the rather fuzzy triggering and messy drum sounds, but gliding and filter control was much more versatile than anything else around at the time, I felt, and you could sustain notes for about 5 hours. The tune was not written especially for the "Acid At The PC Show" demo, having being composed around 8 weeks earlier, but Shane (coder) wanted to use them." (BH) Real name is David Hayes, but always used Ben as nickname. All comments by David "Ben" Hayes are marked with (BH).

Fly By Night Paul Hardcastle "Oh dear! Let's face it, Neil Baldwin did the best C64 version of this ever, and it was foolish to try and emulate it... This was done on SoedeSoft (I think) at 5am on the Sunday morning of the 1989 PC Show in London (hence the demo title). Has a long ending after a drum solo that John Bonham would probably laugh at. I also did a version of this tune in Ubiks Music in 1988, which was even worse. I hope that's never found!" (BH) Real name is David Hayes, but always used Ben as nickname. Ocean Loader 1 Martin Galway "Just done to test out the System 6581 editor, which I'd just got - and this is one of my very favourite C64 tunes ever. It was never meant to be released but we ended up sticking in on an SG demo disk anyway. Note that one of the arpeggios is a bit wonky, and I couldn't be bothered to do the start of the piece, but I felt that it was a pretty good sound-a-like." "Another day, another pointless budget game. Yogi Bear deserved better! I can't remember if I composed the tune or if it was a conversion of some Atari ST music, written by some bloke who's name I can't remember. We used to do a few conversions back then. These were great fun to do. The software company would sent Gerard Gourley a copy of the original music, usually recorded on a cassette recorder sitting by the TV. He'd then play the tune down the telephone to me, and I'd record it on another cassette from the telephone's earpiece. The resulting hi-fidelity master recording would then be my basis. I usually had to guess at the basslines, as they'd become totally inaudible on the tape. Then I'd U-U the result back to Gerard within 2 hours, and if I was lucky I'd get £100 about 6 months later after the 'middle man' had taken his bit. Or half that if the tune was for Ocean." (BH) Real name is David Hayes, but always used Ben as nickname. All comments by David "Ben" Hayes are marked with (BH).

"Some people claim that everything imaginable has been done on the C64. This is true to a certain extent. The typical scenario is indeed that you come up with something new just to find out that someone else has done it 10 years ago... But sometimes strange things happen and even lamers like myself stumble on new stuff. This happened when we were working on our 4k intro Pico! for Breakpoint this year. I was coding the music player and tried to create some drum sounds when I accidentally got some harsh, very distorted sounds. The funny thing was that I was using the noise waveform and got something that sounded like a synthesized electric guitar!" (SounDemoN)

entries.s: "1943 was the first commercial game I wrote the music for, and was responsible for me being offered the job at Tiertex. The people who wrote 1943 were John Prince and Donald ?????? (sorry can't remember his last name). They partnered up and started Tiertex in 1987/8, and offered me the job as musician. There were only 5 of us in the company at that time, and we were writing only for Capcom/US Gold, working mainly on arcade conversions." "Human Killing Machine was my attempt to write a soundtrack that sounded like Martin's Comic Bakery. Depending on which review you read, it was either pretty good or the worst music anyone had ever programmed on the C64. :)" (MT) Comic Bakery, Tune #1 Martin Galway The whole music shows a big resemblance to this tune, especially the bassline and the arpeggios. "I will freely admit to Rob Hubbard and Martin Galway being my biggest influences of the time (as far as computer games were concerned), and I will not deny at all that their music had a certain influence on me. I truly wish however, that no-one thinks that I was ever copying them. If any of their sounds or productions in general rubbed off on me, I can only hope that they thought of me as a fan, and not as a plagarist." The actual C64 game was not written by Tiertex (although the other versions were), it was a guy called Chris someone. As I remember, he credited everyone but me!" (MT) (Chris someone = Chris Butler) "ThunderBlade is another favourite and one I loved doing. We got the proper arcade machine into the office to play with. The title music was a little different, no four-to-the-floor, a little more fluty. Then the in-game music just takes over. [...] the game was pretty good, and I made the music sound as much like helicopter blades as possible. I was really pleased with it, and as I recall, ZZap!64 gave it a pretty good score, too." "I had been commissioned by Orpheus Software (ironically the makers of Electrosound) to code the music for their game Sky Runner. They sent me a work-in-progress version of the game along with a sort-of-completed Electrosound composition. They wanted me to transpose this to a non-Electrosound version and make it my own - what you hear on here is the end result. Unfortunately the MD of Orpheus at the time was a complete nightmare to work with - I was young and naive at the time but this was my first experience, commercially, of trying to get money out of someone. He just wouldn't pay - kept saying cheque would be in the post, give it another week or so etc etc....looking at Sky Runner for the first time ever (on [CSDb.dk]) it looks like the programmer's deal with Orpheus went pretty sour as well. I see the game was published by another software house (Cascade?) and the music had gone back to it's original Electrosound composition - obviously I had no dealings with Cascade - they probably didn't even know about my arrangement!!.... About 1 year later, under new management, Orpheus approached me again asking me to do some more music. OK, I said, firstly you pay me for Sky Runner and secondly I want the money for the new music (I think it was an adaption of some board game involving moving buses around London???) up front - they obliged so there was a happy ending to this story." (ST) The original tune can be found in /GAMES/S-Z/Sky_Runner.sid Comments from Stuart Taylor are denoted (ST).

This tune was the original prototype for the title theme from Savage. Jeroen did this first, sampling the Dutch comedian Harry Vermeegen. 'Koud he' was his catchphrase and translated it means 'Cold eh?'. His most notorious use of this was a Dutch TV programme called 'Pisa' (filmed from the leaning tower) with Harry saying his 'Koud He?' catchphrase to everyone that went by. Probe Software then heard the tune and asked Jeroen if he'd change the samples, and lo and behold it became the Savage theme. "Some background info. The 'KOUD HE' sample is from a Dutch comedian called 'Harry Vermeegen'. It was like a hype saying. I found it a nice sample to play around with. A spontanious tune I did just 4 fun." (JT) Comments by Jeroen Tel himself are denoted (JT).

Most of the tunes are heavily inspired by the music in the arcade game. "Turbo Outrun took about a month all together. It was a lot of fun, but I recomposed every tune about three times to get it perfect. I still think it is one of the best audio tracks I ever did on the C64." "One nice, very nice note: 'Turbo Outrun' (the music) has won the: 'Best music on 8bit computer 1989' award at the PCW show (now ECTS) in London. :D Too bad I had to find out later. US Gold received the actual award. Bastards! I wasn't even at the scene when it was presented. :( " (JT) Intro Magical Sound Shower [from the arcade game Out Run] Hiroshi Kawaguchi (Hiro/SEGA Sound Team) Featuring the sampled voice of Jeroen Tel himself. entries.s: Penny Lane [from Magical Mystery Tour] The Beatles These tunes come from a disk from the Dutch Dream Team. An old member of TDT informed us, that they could have been made by Eric (T.E.M), who lived in Apeldoorn/NL. So far only one of these tunes has been found used in a demo and it was credited to "RvLoon Software", hence moved out to /DEMOS/M-R/Rider_in_the_Sky.sid. It is unknown if that credit is real, or if also all these tunes were made by the same author. If you have any info regarding this, please email the HVSC crew.

Despite popular belief, the Amiga version of the tune by Chris Hülsbeck is the cover of this C64 original (done by Ramiro), not vice versa. "Walker's Warbles" was a Martin Walker music demo which came as a free giveaway with the disk version of "Armalyte" by Thalamus (which MW did the music for.) Tune #3 is an early version of what would eventually be used in the game "Dominion" bundled on a Zzap! 64 covertape in 1990, and tune #4 is an early version of the "Aggressor Theme". The final version of this (and the one which Revolution uses) is the one on MW's "Zzap! 64 Music Demo" which appeared on Zzap 64's June 1989 covermount cassette. (Comment by Warren Pilkington) This tune was also used in a game called Revolution (written by Simon Pick). The game was never released, but featured on Commodore Format magazine's powerpack (tape) number one. ### /MUSICIANS/W/Walker_Terry ################################################

Sensoria [from Micro-Phonies] Cabaret Voltaire Based more on the 12" single version, which appears as a bonus track on the CD version of the album. "I've always been a big fan of Cabaret Voltaire, and the 12" version of Sensoria is right up there with my favourites. I'd tried to do a version of it back in 2009, but didn't get beyond the first 30 seconds or so. It was good to go back and start from scratch, and concentrate first on getting the basslines right, and from there build the tune up. It also plays a little bit faster than the original does to keep it faster paced too. Naturally the bass sounds massively better on a 6581 for which the tune was designed, on an 8580 it just doesn't work so well." (WP) All Warren's comments are indicated by (WP). entries.t: We Are Number One but C64 Style
