1999 [from the XM module] Jeroen Tel (WAVE) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Action Biker, Tune #1 Rob Hubbard "This is a remix from Rob Hubbard's Action Biker main theme (tune #1) from the year 1985! (C) Mastertronic. Listen to the original and hear the difference! I first typed over the notes (bass + lead) from a Music Assembler example tune. Not using the ugly percussion track. The chords are typed over from a Midi file called Biker. (Lazy me eh?!). Maybe this will not be necessary in future because there is a Midi to Mod program and buddy Roland Hermans has made a Mod to Sid program. I'm not quite happy with this tune because of the weak 2 notes arpeggio part (from 1:14 to 1:50). I made the volume of this arpeggio part a bit softer so it becomes a bit less annoying. Maybe I will improve this tune sometime. Same presets used as in Rolfie Title Remix. Typing over the notes took some amount of time (I always work slowly!). I used too many sequences in the 2nd track (it can only handle 128). So Roland Hermans "packed" several sequences into only a few so the player can handle them. This is the 2nd tune for mainly Polish based group Axelerate. Tune is played at CIA 1 Timer A (PAL) because we wanted another speed than a normal one. Tune has nice ending, don't you agree? Hope you like it!" (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

"I went into this project wanting to write a "classic" SID that people want to listen to frequently perhaps even like a good 80s game SID. Soon I noticed I had too few good ideas myself so I used some "borrowed" music in this one in true Rob Hubbard style (he also covered a lot as you know). So some of other composer's music was the basis of some tunes varied with own ideas and combinations of these 2. Of course Roland Hermans (Neo) helped me with the technical bits." (JW) Intro Tune "The short intro jingle still went some work in it being quite complex. The end sounds particularly well with that kick sound attached to the bass." (JW) The War Begins Spybreak! [from Decksandrumsandrockandroll] (1:16-2:33) Propellerheads "As you can hear in The War Begins I like the Matt Gray style. It's simple to do and still sounds great. The combination with the Matrix tune works well I think. Also I listened to a lot of hard rock/heavy metal music to get inspired. A lot of what Matt Gray did can be identified with this style. Using double bass plus MG drums is a good combination plus after that a ring modulation lead sounds nice." (JW) Massive Attack "Massive Attack begins with 2 tracks shooting SFX from the game Dominator. Then a Star Wars alike film tune. The piece after that the Jon Dunn's Robocop lead instrument fits and sounds so well! Some funny kicks and snares in different volumes. The last piece is very short 'n simple and still sounds good. Only a few sequences used. About 4 if I remember well." (JW) Arduous Battle "Arduous Battle is completely done by me. In a lot of places the bass notes are harder on the beat. In this I made a 64 version of a tune I composed on the Amiga with Protracker which was called Freedom. What I really like about this tune is the end part which was also first composed on the Amiga." (JW) The Tragic One "Sniff sniff! A very melancholic beginning. Then some sort of Philip Glass stuff which ends with an attempt to do something similar to Hubbard's

"Own composed in true JW style! To get going making midi files I'm making a midi cover of this. I'd better make those chords notes slower (I want to go towards making music for a band). Instead of using slides I used Dane's technique (in Whistle song): a length 1 note for some lead notes. Used as Turn disk music in my 1st music colly." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Passacaglia <?> "A partial cover of a music which was one of the demo tunes in the Amiga music program Deluxe Music Construction Set. Bass resembles a bit the first part of House of the Rising Sun by The Animals when the singing starts. Used as jiffy sound on my 1st music colly!" (JW) Yogi Bear Song Hoyt Stoddard Curtin (music), William Hanna & Joseph Barbera (lyrics) "From the animated TV series "Yogi Bear" composed in 1960. This was harder to convert than I expected. I asked some acquaintances to help me out but they couldn't. So I did it myself and there are no off key notes in this! Presets are from Parasol Stars tunes. An mp3 was the example for this. Used as Title tune of my 1st music colly!" (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

"Demo containing this tune had a nice "gadget" enclosed. The drive led reacted on 1 of the tracks. (Ofcourse coded by Roland Hermans). I only just came up with the title of this song after Roland changed something in the presets (instruments) which gave it an Arabian touch. Ok I think. Composed on piano." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

entries.t: As de sterre dao baove straole
entries.s: As de sterre dao baove straole Arthur "Thuur" Luxembourg (music), Frans Boermans (lyrics) "The demo in which this sound was spread contained the full lyrics of the song written in South Dutch dialect. This tune consists of a double lead to get a sort of echo effect. The reason why I made this song: In the south of Holland we celibrate Carnival each year around the end of February and because I live in a provence of Southern Holland called Limburg I decided to make one of the best Carnival songs on the C64! During Carnival everyone dresses up in some strange costume and goes into pubs to party and of course drink a lot of beer. The title of the song translated into English is: When the stars are shining up there. Written in waltz tempo. Hope you like it." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).
All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

press fire [from the Amiga game Shadow of the Beast III] Tim Wright "Of course I had to squeeze the Amiga 4 tracks in to C64's 3. But the tune uses 2 tracks for the part which isn't the lead or bass. How do you call that part anyway? (backing?) While going through old Amiga 500 games with buddy Roland (we were looking through because we are planning a C64 demo consisting converted Amiga pics in FLI-Interlace) we stumbled upon this tune. I like it very much so I tried if I could rip it with my Datel Electronics' Amiga Action Replay MK III. I froze the game and typed in tracker. And golly yes! The cartridge found the tune and I saved it to disc and loaded it in my Protracker soundtool. Together with Roland I converted it. (He works much quicker than me). We are planning to do more conversions. After this conversion Roland made a program to convert from MOD to SID, right into my player as I said in Action Biker Remix STIL text. But now it even converts arpeggios! The presets are: bass from Psycho Pigs UXB. Flute resembles Amiga lead sample instrument but has a little waveform 41 tick at the beginning and is made by Roland. Other preset is from Henning Rokling's Henning_Rokling-02.sid which is used in demo Wild At Heart. We first made an arpeggio sound consisting of two different c notes but it didn't work out well. In beginning of the tune you can hear a build up of decay and sustain in this preset. To get this effect we had to make 4 presets just changing the decay and sustain from 2 to 8. The wave on effects on bass and Rokling preset make it sound ok on C64. Often this effect is used to substitute normal hi hat sounds. This ditty is one of my favourite tunes!" (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Because I Got High Afroman "Before I saw the movie Jay & Silent Bob Strike back (this zax was the end music of the hilarious film) I wanted to make a cover of this afrolicious tune! It's probably the only tune they made which is cool. This C64 version is a bit faster, probably in an other key and is fast composed. The arpeggio lead was taken from my Space Harrier Remix. Respect!" (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Blackadder [from the TV series] Howard Goodall "The one that drove JW insane was Blackadder Theme. I was looking and looking for bass notes but never found any that sounded good! So I decided to let them out and use 2 voices for the lead. The idea to make this mini tune was that I coincidentally found a nice midi file on the net from which I only used the background. Preset of this is taken from Demon's Aural Manouvers II. I listened to the original TV theme on the BBC and was surprised to find out that I liked this version more than the original!" (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Stille Nacht! Heilige Nacht! Joseph Mohr (lyrics), Franz Xaver Gruber (music) "This little zax was hence the name especially made for a man I know from my home village who collects all existing versions of the Silent Night tune. This tune was used in a Covenant demo for the X-mas competition 2003." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

"Game was made (like Tough Guys) by Ramon (BB) van de Laar. And it's about a forester who has to paint the brown leaves green again avoiding EVIL forest animals. It was a real pain in the ass to play but was awarded as one of the best games in '92. My pally Roland Hermans (ex-Einstein/RGJ/Smidas from ATG (Actual Trading Generation) always helped me with the technical bits of C64 music like players and presets etc. Some presets throughout this game music are from Johannes Bjerregaard's Flimbo's Quest. There's one I used as lead, bass and as arpeggio (chords)." (JW) "This is the congratulations tune consisting a Follin like melody row of fast notes made by Roland Hermans. The filter lead in the beginning is from Jeroen Tel's Myth tune #3. As you can hear I very much like to leave the bass away at the end of zaxes to get a nice "echo" effect." (JW) "This level tune #1, a 2-voice zax made in a simple march tempo. The other track was used as sound-fx track. I thought about putting in a 3rd optional drum track or extra lead track but this was thought to be not necessary." (JW) "This is the second level zax, also 2-voiced. Bit more cheerful than the 1st level zax. Bits of the melody popped into my mind when I was cycling home from school." (JW) Canon in D major Johann Pachelbel "I used a Tim Follin bass from Psycho Pigs UXB tune #1. The harmonica is from Follin's Black Lamp, Tune #1." (JW) "This is the game over tune. First made in Dutch USA team's Music Assembler. I made this tune not knowing what it would become. But it fits its purpose very nicely I think." (JW) "This is the high score tune. Before Forester this sound was published (slightly different from this one) as "Ode to Junior". Junior was a cat that we had at my elderly home. Was, because he's now in cat's heaven. Tune was made in a period I didn't know how to make use of arpeggio's (chord substitutes). It's still ok, I guess." (JW) "This is the bonus level tune. It's made a bit faster than the level tunes to ge

High Score [from the Game Boy game Tetris] Hirokazu Tanaka (Hip) "This is 1 of my 2 all time Game Boy favorites, the 1st is of course Super Mario Land. This zax has the same structure as Blackadder Theme but the lead in Blackadder is more fluty. The midi tune I found on the net had some faults in it. But they were soon ironed out by me." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Opening/Closing [from Glassworks] Philip Glass "This is my 2nd Glass cover and there will follow more. This is converted from a midi file I found on the net. All presets are the same but the bass preset is a bit softer. This preset is from Jonathan Dunn's Robocop. Very nice pulse thingy in it. The lead from 1:55 is done by me." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).
All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Blade Runner (End Titles) [from the movie] Vangelis "This zax is a Matt Gray alike version of Bladerunner end titles, hence the name. It was used in one of JSL's entries for the gfx competition on Vision 2003. I thought a nice picture needs a nice sound. Pity the music was not played during the gfx compo. This was changed in comparison with last year's party. Bass preset is from a Boogaloo sound, Matt Gray drums were surprisingly not taken from one of his sounds but from a Fanta tune, lead done by Roland. First use of ring modulation of this kind in a tune by me!" (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Reyn Ouwehand's version also has its moments. Though I think my version has the most resembling saxophone sound on this compy." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Koyaanisqatsi [from the movie] Philip Glass "Glass' own style is called "minimalistic music". I got the music on tape from pally Paultje (M0k) Kessels, I thought it was brill and converted it into Dutch USA team's Music Assembler. Bass is nice, original MA drums are awful." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Kung Fu Fighting [from Kung Fu Fighting] Carl Douglas "This is what you get when you have to make a tune on a party (Vision 2002) in a hurry without a keyboard! Exile/Anubis made a pic of a toy hamster singing this song. (one of the compo prizes). That's why I made this. I changed the text which is in the beginning of this tune at $1000 into: please don't rip this music etc. But yeah! those guys of the HVSC crew want every SID ever made in the HVSC. So that's why it's in here! Oh sigh!" (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Lady Modjo "Modjo made a cover of Chic's Soup For One from 1982. Composers were Bernard Edwards and Nile Rodgers. Modjo's version is much faster. Something which you see more lately in covers. This music was made for D-Pac, he made a textro to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the 64! It was released on 19th of October 2002 at the special edition of the Dutch HCC computer show. As you can hear this sound uses a 2 tracks snare which was taken from Tim Follin's Qix. Hope U like it!" (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

"This game was a conversion of a popular word game on tv in Holland and even was sometime in Germany on the telly in which you get one letter of the 5 or 6 and have to guess which word it is, roughly said. It's been on the Dutch telly for years and years now, and still is very popular. Game was coded by pally Roland Hermans. And the music consists of several covers." (JW) Ritmo de la Noche Mystic "This is the title theme and means in English: Rhythm of the night. Mystic's version was based on: I go to Rio from Peter Allen and Ritmo de la Noche by Chocolate. It contains 5 tracks: 3 normal and 2 separate digi tracks consisting of a drum track and some several chords track. Was first made with Protracker on my old and trusty Amiga 500." (JW) "The row of notes (not the bass or lead) is borrowed from a music I heard in the heroic cartoon series Prince Valiant and is used as high score music. It consists again a bass from Tim Follin's Psycho Pigs UXB tune #1. Lead is again of Jeroen Tel's Myth tune #3 this time without filter. Of course the old trick is used to divide the notes over 2 tracks." (JW) I Promised Myself [from Move Until We Fly] (1:01-1:47) Nick Kamen "This is the ingame music and consists of 3 parts: The first I wrote myself, and the 3rd is also self made, hear that super fast bass! The second part is a cover, mentioned above." (JW) Hazard Richard Marx "This is the game over tune. Also first use of slide effects (portamento) in my music to give that extra edge." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

"Called sleeping song because Roland thought it was a song from which you get very sleepy. The chords are taken from the beginning of the music of a Dutch USA team demo called Nemesis, I made use of some sawtooth presets to get that Galway feel. Bassline is simply using a C note and the C note an octave higher. Made in Music Assembler which was shortened by pally Roland Hermans, so it only occupies memory from $1000-$12EF on the C64 which is 3 blocks (less than 1 K!). Neil Baldwin's Music Demo Number One was an example for me, using 2 tracks for lead when the bass is suspended. The nicest thing of the C64 SID chip is that you can create a warm analogue sound." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).
"An experimental piece. This was the least bad version. Composed on piano and by voice." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

"Look at text enclosed with Merlin's Dream. Music is the same but the sample beat was removed and replaced by normal C64 drums which were attached to the bass notes. This tune was used in diskmag Arachnophobia #21." (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

titlemusic v2 [from the Amiga game Double Dragon III] (2:48-3:57) Andrew Barnabas (Night-Shade) "This is my Mekka Symposium 2001 SID competition entry. It finished 11th from the 29 and got 32 votes. Too bad there is no independent jury on the Mekka party so if you know a lot of people who will vote for you, you will finish 1st. The first part (from 0:00 to 0:45) was made back in '92. The rest was made in 2 weeks in 2001. At the party SIDs are played up to 4 minutes. So I had to stop at the end of the 4th minute. Since this msx contains a sample beat it must be played on an old SID, as was done on the party. You had to mention on the entry sheet which SID they had to use. Too bad the music was played too soft on the party (held during Easter). The zax might be a bit too long-winded. The DD III part was converted from an Amiga MOD" (JW) The Double Dragon III music is better known by its real name of Water II and was one of the tracks on Andrew Barnabas' CD. All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

Parasol Stars Boss [from the PC Engine game] Turbo Mira, Yasuko "This is like the Ingame tune a conversion of an Amiga Octamed file I found on the net. Same presets used as in the Ingame tune. "This is a remix of the title theme I made for a children's cd rom I am making together with some pallies of mine. So in total there are 12 different country drawings, a title page, a credits page and and end page. With every page there comes an appropriate, spheric music plus lyrics about what can be seen in the drawings. All the sight seeing objects can be seen in a picture of each country. For instance in Egypt you can see: some pyramids, a sphinx, the Nile, a palm tree, some background items and Rolfie the cat on a camel. When you click on an object it starts to animate and a WAV-file begins to play making e.g. a camel sound and telling a story about e.g. a camel. This title tune is apart from the melody altered heavily to let it sound ok on the C64. This is the first tune I made since 1992 which was spread, so you can call it a sort of test tune. And this is also the first tune made for mainly Poland based group Axelerate which has died in the beginning of 2001. All presets are the same as in Linko music except before every bass sound (from 0:15), there is a kick drum sound added. Idea for 3 track chords in beginning is from Reyn Ouwehand's Deadlock (brilliant title tune). Wind sound was added, as always if something needs to be added, it was done by pally Roland 'Neo' Hermans. Hope U like it!" (JW) All comments by Joachim Wijnhoven are marked with (JW).

"It's a long time ago that I composed sounds for the good old C64. But all I remember is that it was a very great time with much fun. My composing started in the years 1983/84 when I programmed my own music-editor and the music-play-routine. I made an extra-routine for each sound. From music to music I changed that routine to get different sounds. I have made some musics, good and bad sounds. But I have tried to make people happy with listening to my music." (Comment by Winterberg himself.)
